title: Error Practice
goal: In this lesson you will practice spotting, catching, and fixing errors in short programs.
learn: Fix root causes when you can
idea: Practice time! Sometimes you fix the bug (best). Sometimes you catch a risk you cannot avoid (like bad text becoming a number). Read the message, choose fix vs catch, and keep the program kind to the next kid who runs it.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first value from "10" to "5". Press Run. First result should be 20.0.

practice.text: Loop ['3','0','x']. For each, try 9/int(item). Catch ValueError and ZeroDivisionError with different messages.
practice.hint: Inside try:, compute print(9 / int(item)). "3" works, "0" hits ZeroDivisionError, "x" hits ValueError — give each except its own message.
practice.starterTip: In try: add print(9 / int(item)). In except blocks try print("Not a number!") and print("Cannot divide by zero!").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 3.0 prints, zero-divide is caught, and x triggers ValueError message.

practice.text: Fix the NameError (do not use try). Print the sum of a and b.
practice.hint: There is no variable c — only a and b exist. The sum of 4 and 6 should be 10.
practice.starterTip: Change print(a + c) to print(a + b) — no try/except needed, just fix the typo.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if print uses a + b and shows 10 with no error.

quiz.question: When should you fix instead of catch?

options.text: When the bug is a simple mistake you control

quiz.correct: Typos should be fixed; risky input may be caught.

quiz.question: Can one try have more than one except?
quiz.wrong: ValueError and ZeroDivisionError can both appear.

quiz.question: What is the goal of error practice?

options.text: Programs that fail softly and stay clear

project.title: Error Detective
project.desc: Build a tiny tool that tries to convert each of '8', '0', 'hi' and print 16/n. Use specific excepts. End with All checked.
